articles.title: Women more drawn to hypothetical jobs where most employees were women
articles.summary: Women were more interested in hypothetical jobs, and expected to feel more at home in them, when told most employees were women, according to four studies that pitted gender representation against job ads emphasizing brilliance.

articles.title: Emotional blunting is common in depression and bipolar disorder, even after symptoms ease
articles.summary: Recovering from depression doesn’t always mean feeling things fully again. In a study of 106 patients on antidepressants, emotional blunting was less common among patients in remission but still affected 45% of them.

articles.title: How your personality “acts as an invisible architect for your career,” according to new research
articles.summary: Are you willing to wait for a bigger payoff? Researchers studying young Danes found that the more patient ones tended to apply to longer degree programs with steeper earnings growth, even after accounting for grades and family background.

articles.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
articles.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

articles.title: What happens in the brain when cannabis makes you anxious?
articles.summary: Cannabinoids may intensify anxiety by removing a natural brake on specific neurons in the brain’s fear center, particularly during stressful situations. In mice, shutting down those neurons sharply reduced cannabinoid-related anxious behavior.

articles.title: The invisible chore that may matter more for women’s relationship happiness than housework
articles.summary: Both men and women agree that women carry more of a household’s mental load. A new study finds that women report greater satisfaction when it’s shared equally, while men report greater relationship satisfaction when their partners carry more.

articles.title: Childhood ADHD diagnosis linked to lower adult religious attendance
articles.summary: A childhood ADHD diagnosis is linked to a steep decline in adult religious service attendance, especially among Black and Asian American adults. Private spiritual practices like prayer, however, remain largely unaffected by the neurodevelopmental condition.

articles.title: Which cities dominated 2020 voter fraud talk? A city’s Black population was the best predictor
articles.summary: After the 2020 election, online talk of voter fraud zeroed in on cities with large Black populations. A new study suggests these racialized claims found a particularly receptive audience among White Americans who score high in racial resentment.

articles.title: Researchers explore how J-Pop listening habits impact visual memory
articles.summary: A small pilot study explored whether listening to favorite pop songs helps or hinders visual memory. Brain scans suggest preferred music might support attention, but larger studies are needed to verify these preliminary findings.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
articles.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials. Researchers say regulated vaping products are not risk-free, but may be a significantly less harmful alternative for people who would otherwise continue smoking.

articles.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
articles.summary: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders. The discovery could help researchers repurpose existing drugs for conditions including traumatic brain injury, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, depression, and schizophrenia.

articles.title: Synthesis Through Simulation: Generating Coherent Enterprise Data via Scalable Agent-System Interaction
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.10549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-calling agents have become central to enterprise AI, yet training and evaluating them at scale remains severely constrained due to business and legal restrictions on enterprise systems, data, and database schemas. Tabular data synthesis offers a natural alternative, but its effectiveness is fundamentally limited by structural validity and schema availability, while procedure-based approaches yield the opposite weakness, typically lacking distributional fidelity without per-domain authoring. We introduce **Synthesis Through Simulation** (STS)

articles.title: Agent-Controlled Forgetting for Tool-Using Agents: Reversible Context Curation in Practice
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.10590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using agents repeatedly carry observations whose useful content can be much smaller than their original payload. We study agent-controlled forgetting: the acting model selects previously observed tool results, replaces each with a short note at its original position, and retains the exact original in a recoverable archive. A Python harness exposes batch archival and explicit recovery without task-specific model training, while protecting user instructions and assistant messages from these operations.
